What it generally means: Moisture is generally adequate, but the growing season is cool and relatively short.
Moisture and temperature generally favor annual cereal production where soils and topography allow cultivation.
Deep soils usually recharge in most years, allowing annual cropping in most years. Fallow may be useful in drier years.
Shallow soils usually refill during winter, so summer fallow provides little additional water-storage benefit.
Winter precipitation is often not enough to refill the deep soil profile. Summer fallow can help store water for the following crop.
Low precipitation and hot conditions generally make irrigation necessary for dependable crop production.
